reported.title: Drip pulses fire back-to-back instead of every 800 ms
reported.description: The scheduler stores the next due time in an 8-bit variable (line 10) and computes it as `(uint8_t)(now8 + PERIOD_MS)` on lines 56 and 73, so 800 ms wraps modulo 256 to 32 ms. The due check on line 71 then re-triggers almost immediately after each pulse ends, producing the measured gaps of 49-50 ms between `drip` lines instead of 800 ms. The `now8 >= nextDue` comparison also breaks across the 255->0 rollover, giving the observed worst gaps of 387-705 ms. Expected /^drip$/ every 800 ± 120 ms; 103 of 105 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 705 ms.

judge_input.spec:
- Drip solenoid driver on D8; pause button on D4 to ground with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Emit a 50 ms HIGH pulse on D8 every 800 ms while pause is released.
- Print the exact line `drip` at the start of each pulse; period must stay 800 ms ±120 ms.
- While D4 is held LOW, suppress new pulses and keep D8 LOW.
- Every 1600 ms print `drip n=<count> pause=<0|1>`.
- Stay responsive: complete each pulse without multi-second blocking waits.
